t.3.53.1: Having given his orders to the eight terrible rākṣasas of great strength, Rāvaṇa, through the confusion of his mind, considered himself to have accomplished his purpose.
t.3.53.2: Thinking of Vaidehī, pierced by the arrows of desire, he entered his delightful house, hastening eagerly to see Sītā.
t.3.53.3: Having entered that dwelling, Rāvaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, saw Sītā amid the Rākṣasī women, wholly given over to grief.
t.3.53.4: Her face filled with tears, wretched and crushed beneath the weight of grief, she was like a ship sinking in the ocean, overwhelmed by the force of the winds.
t.3.53.5: And the night-wanderer, drawing near to her, who was like a doe strayed from the herd and surrounded by dogs, her face cast down and wretched,
t.3.53.6: But the lord of the Rākṣasas forcibly showed her, wretched, helpless, and overcome by grief, his house, which was like the dwelling of the gods.
t.3.53.7: It was crowded with mansions and palaces, frequented by thousands of women, thronged by flocks of many kinds of birds, and filled with gems of every sort.
t.3.53.8: With pillars of gold and of refined gold, of crystal and likewise of silver, variegated with diamonds and cat's-eye gems, delightful to the eye.
t.3.53.9: Together with her he climbed the wondrous golden staircase, which resounded with the sound of celestial drums and was adorned with archways of refined gold.
t.3.53.10: There were windows made of ivory and of silver, delightful to behold and covered with golden latticework, and there stood rows of palaces.
t.3.53.11: In his own palace Daśagrīva showed Maithilī the floor areas on every side, variegated with stucco and jewels.
t.3.53.12: The long ponds and lotus pools, covered with flowers of many kinds: these Rāvaṇa showed to Sītā, who was wholly given over to grief.
t.3.53.13: Having shown Vaidehī that entire excellent mansion, the evil-souled Rāvaṇa spoke these words to the daughter of Janaka.
t.3.53.14: Ten crores of rākṣasas, and another twenty-two crores besides, leaving aside the night-rangers who are bent with old age and those who are children.
t.3.53.15: O Sītā, I am the lord of all those of dreadful deeds; a full thousand of them wait upon me alone, ever foremost in carrying out my tasks.
t.3.53.17: Of the many thousands of women who make up my household, be you the mistress, O Sītā; become my wife, beloved.
t.3.53.16: This entire kingdom and its governance of mine, and my very life, all rest upon you, O large-eyed one; you are dearer to me than my own life-breaths.
t.3.53.19: This Laṅkā, a hundred yojanas in extent, is encircled by the ocean; it cannot be assailed even by the gods and asuras together with Indra.
t.3.53.18: It is fitting; what use to you is any other thought? Accept my words. Be mine; you ought to show favour to me, who am tormented.
t.3.53.20: Neither among the Devas nor among the Yakṣas, neither among the Gandharvas nor among the Ṛṣis, nor anywhere in the worlds do I see anyone who could be my equal in valour.
t.3.53.21: What will you do with Rāma, a mere man of little power, wretched, fallen from his kingdom, an ascetic whose life is already spent?
t.3.53.23: Do not set your mind on seeing Rāghava, O lovely-faced one. What power has he, O Sītā, to come here, even in his wildest dreams?
t.3.53.22: Accept me alone, Sītā, for I am a husband worthy of you. Youth is fleeting and fearful; take your delight here with me.
t.3.53.25: In all the three worlds, O lovely one, I see no one who could carry you off by force while you are protected by my arms.
t.3.53.24: The wind of great speed cannot be bound with nooses in the sky, nor can one grasp the pure flame of a blazing fire.
t.3.53.26: Rule over this very great kingdom in Laṅkā; and, drenched with the waters of consecration and content, give me delight.
t.3.53.27: Whatever evil deed you did in the past has been spent through your dwelling in the forest; now obtain here the fruit of the righteousness you have well performed.
t.3.53.28: Here are all garlands of heavenly fragrance, O Maithilī, and the finest ornaments; enjoy them together with me.
t.3.53.29: O lady of lovely hips, the aerial chariot named Puṣpaka belonged to my brother Vaiśravaṇa; that chariot is delightful and swift as thought.
t.3.53.30: There, O Sītā, sport with me as you please. Your face is like a lotus, spotless and lovely to behold.
t.3.53.31: Stricken with grief, your face does not shine, O lady of lovely hips, O fair-faced one. Enough of this shame of yours, Vaidehī, born of the fear of breaking dharma.
t.3.53.32: This outpouring of destiny that will come upon you is sanctioned by the seers. These tender feet of yours are pressed by me with my heads.
t.3.53.33: Grant me your favour quickly; I am your obedient slave. These words spoken by me, who am wasting away with longing, are not empty.
t.3.53.34: And Rāvaṇa would never bow his head to any woman. Having spoken thus, the ten-necked one addressed Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka,
t.3.53.35: Fallen into the power of Death, he thinks, "She is mine."
